title: Modi Urges 'Vocal for Local' Festive Buying in 139th Mann Ki Baat
excerpt: In the 139th Mann Ki Baat, PM Modi cited makhana exports to Greece, pulses to the Maldives and Rs 28 crore in single-day Khadi sales as he asked shoppers to back local artisans ahead of Diwali and Chhath.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi used the 139th Mann Ki Baat, marking 12 years of the broadcast, to urge festive shoppers to prioritise products made by local artisans ahead of Diwali and Chhath.
  • Modi cited Purnia makhana from Bihar reaching Greece and Kalaburagi arhar dal from Karnataka being exported to the Maldives as evidence that Vocal for Local is opening world markets for Indian farmers.
  • Khadi Gram Udyog sales exceeded Rs 28 crore in a single day on Gandhi Jayanti, up Rs 1.5 crore from the previous year, according to the address.
  • The broadcast also covered the IIT Madras brain centre, Maharashtra tribal packaging that won Japan's Good Design Award, and revivals of organic cotton in Punjab and millets in the Northeast.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday urged citizens to buy products made by local artisans and strengthen the Vocal for Local campaign as India prepares to celebrate Diwali and Chhath, saying the preference for indigenous goods is now taking Indian products to markets around the world.

In the 139th episode of his monthly radio programme Mann Ki Baat, which marked 12 years since the broadcast began on Vijayadashami, Modi said shoppers had already begun giving more importance to indigenous products during the festive season. According to The Hindu BusinessLine, he framed that shift as a direct route to Atmanirbhar Bharat, or a self-reliant India.

"This spirit of 'Vocal for Local' is now taking our products to global markets."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister

Farm produce cited as export proof

Modi gave two farm examples to support the claim. Makhana, or foxnut, from Purnia in Bihar is now reaching Greece, and arhar dal from Kalaburagi in Karnataka is being exported to the Maldives, he said, according to ANI reporting carried by NewKerala. "New markets are opening up in the world for the farmers of India," he said.

He also pointed to value addition and packaging. In Maharashtra, tribal communities marketing honey, mahua, chironji and bamboo products through Shabari Naturals use packaging that carries tribal art, and that packaging has received Japan's Good Design Award. A Karnataka start-up, he added, is making packaging material from bamboo and agricultural residue.

Khadi provided the sales figure in the address. Sales of Khadi Gram Udyog products exceeded Rs 28 crore in a single day on Gandhi Jayanti this year, Rs 1.5 crore more than the previous year, Modi said. He linked the rise to artisans and handicraft workers whose skills produce the goods.

"During festivals, we buy many things for our families and loved ones. This time too, when you shop, please prioritise products made by local artisans."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister

Beyond shopping: farms, millets and research

The address ranged beyond festive buying. In Punjab's Malwa region, Modi cited Nav-Trinjan, an initiative of the Kheti Virasat Mission that promotes organic cotton cultivation, and said its weaving school has changed the lives of many women. In the Northeast, he described a revival of millet cultivation: two women in Khanduli village in Meghalaya developed millet-based cookies, cakes, muffins and baby food, while Kezoma village in Nagaland resumed millet farming in 2024 after a gap of more than a decade and held its first millet festival in 2025.

Modi also described a visit to Chennai earlier this month, where he inaugurated the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras. The centre is creating high-resolution digital 3D images of the human brain, aims to map 100 human brains in detail using the Param Shakti supercomputer, and will make the data available as an open-source resource, he said. He called it the first mission of its kind in the world and noted that Alzheimer's and dementia still lack a definitive cure. At IIT Madras he also met start-ups working on gold-quality verification, faster recovery of money lost to bank fraud, AI-assisted screening for cervical cancer, a sea-capable electric vehicle, and fast-charging batteries for drones and electric vehicles.

Cleanliness appeal and 12-year milestone

Ahead of Diwali and Chhath, Modi called on citizens to join cleanliness campaigns in their own localities. Leaders and listeners followed the broadcast across the country, including Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi in Bhubaneswar and Union Minister Annapurna Devi with local residents in Ranchi, ANI reported.

Recalling the start of the programme 12 years ago, Modi described Mann Ki Baat as a pilgrimage: a journey to understand the efforts of people across the country and to pay tribute to their contributions. Listeners, he said, had been both fellow travellers and guides throughout.

What it means for diaspora readers

For Indian families abroad shopping for Diwali, the practical takeaway in the address is specific: when buying festive goods, gifts and food products this season, choose items made by local Indian artisans and producers where possible. Modi argued that those purchases directly support artisan incomes at home, while the export examples he cited — makhana to Greece and pulses to the Maldives — show the same products reaching overseas shelves.

The next Mann Ki Baat episode is expected on the last Sunday of next month, following the programme's monthly schedule.
